unlisted_practices: Implement standardized tools to measure AI energy consumption, CO2 emissions, and water usage.
Conduct lifecycle assessments of AI systems and use transparent reporting mechanisms to promote environmental accountability.
Integrate emission calculators and sustainability dashboards into hospital operations to monitor and reduce environmental footprint.
Adopt circular resource practices such as reusing waste heat from AI operations and recycling decommissioned hardware.
Prefer energy-efficient model designs and data compression techniques to reduce the computational costs of AI.
Host AI workloads on cloud infrastructure powered by renewable energy and use advanced cooling technologies and waste heat recovery.
Assess potential performance limitations of energy-efficient AI models such as Tiny AI before high-stakes clinical deployment to ensure energy efficiency does not compromise clinical reliability.
Integrate environmental performance metrics into procurement criteria and accreditation standards for AI.
Governments and health authorities should offer green incentives, subsidies, or tax benefits to hospitals investing in low-carbon digital technologies.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/letter outlining considerations and recommendations for sustainable/green AI implementation and environmental impact monitoring in healthcare.
